title: School marks and skipping grades
summary: A good memory made him a good student; one teacher blocked his skipping two grades, and the graduating class staged dances.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Then I got back home, and continued playing with Don Dunbar during the summer months, and gigged around home...
You were (?) had to go to school.

Oh yeah. I would come back and go to school every year. Sometimes I'd be a little late started, but my teachers, well, they were pretty cool. I was very good in school. I had a good memory. I didn't do too much

studying, but I would come up with those good report cards because I could remember, you know. If I'd hear them say something, you know... I had a good memory. So I was very good in school. In fact, when I got... In fact, I was in the sixth grade, and all of my teachers agreed to let me skip Seven and Eight, and go to the Ninth Grade. All except one, Mrs. Clark. I'll never forget, she told me, she said... "Look," she said, "don't think I'm holding you back, but if you do this, you're going to miss too much, and that won't be good. So I'm not going to agree." And she nixed the whole thing, you know. And I appreciated it, seeing how she said, "No, you'll miss too much," you know.

But I was well-known around through Jackson, you know, and I had... We had staged some dances, the kids at school, we had... When we graduated from the Ninth Grade, we staged some dances and stuff, you know, and had the band playing down there. Our principal at the school, boy, that would be the last thing he'd want to see happen, but we had all of the teachers going for it, so we won him over, after it all happened, you know. He didn't know until it was all over. But he came on in with us, you know.
